title: Berland Local Positioning System
statementMd:
In Berland a bus travels along the main street of the capital. The street begins from the main square and looks like a very long segment. There are $*n*$ bus stops located along the street, the $*i*$-th of them is located at the distance $*a*_{*i*}$ from the central square, all distances are distinct, the stops are numbered in the order of increasing distance from the square, that is, $*a*_{*i*} < *a*_{*i* + 1}$ for all $*i*$ from 1 to $*n* - 1$. The bus starts its journey from the first stop, it passes stops $2$, $3$ and so on. It reaches the stop number $*n*$, turns around and goes in the opposite direction to stop $1$, passing all the intermediate stops in the reverse order. After that, it again starts to move towards stop $*n*$. During the day, the bus runs non-stop on this route.

The bus is equipped with the Berland local positioning system. When the bus passes a stop, the system notes down its number.

One of the key features of the system is that it can respond to the queries about the distance covered by the bus for the parts of its path between some pair of stops. A special module of the system takes the input with the information about a set of stops on a segment of the path, a stop number occurs in the set as many times as the bus drove past it. This module returns the length of the traveled segment of the path (or -1 if it is impossible to determine the length uniquely). The operation of the module is complicated by the fact that *stop numbers occur in the request not in the order they were visited but in the non-decreasing order*.

For example, if the number of stops is $6$, and the part of the bus path starts at the bus stop number $5$, ends at the stop number $3$ and passes the stops as follows: ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f603d9c4afa723f7976dfc0c5250bf25a325383b.png), then the request about this segment of the path will have form: $3, 4, 5, 5, 6$. If the bus on the segment of the path from stop $5$ to stop $3$ has time to drive past the $1$-th stop (i.e., if we consider a segment that ends with the second visit to stop $3$ on the way from $5$), then the request will have form: $1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6$.

You will have to repeat the Berland programmers achievement and implement this function.

## Input

The first line contains integer $*n*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 2·10^{5}$) — the number of stops.

The second line contains $*n*$ integers ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$) — the distance from the $*i*$-th stop to the central square. The numbers in the second line go in the increasing order.

The third line contains integer $*m*$ ($1 ≤ *m* ≤ 4·10^{5}$) — the number of stops the bus visited on some segment of the path.

The fourth line contains $*m*$ integers ($1 ≤ *b*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$) — the sorted list of numbers of the stops visited by the bus on the segment of the path. The number of a stop occurs as many times as it was visited by a bus.

It is guaranteed that the query corresponds to some segment of the path.

## Output

In the single line please print the distance covered by a bus. If it is impossible to determine it unambiguously, print $- 1$.

## Note

The first test from the statement demonstrates the first example shown in the statement of the problem.

The second test from the statement demonstrates the second example shown in the statement of the problem.

In the third sample there are two possible paths that have distinct lengths, consequently, the sought length of the segment isn't defined uniquely.

In the fourth sample, even though two distinct paths correspond to the query, they have the same lengths, so the sought length of the segment is defined uniquely.
statementZhMd:
在伯兰，公交车沿着首都的主街道行驶。这条街道从中央广场开始，看起来像一条非常长的线段。街道上分布着 $*n*$ 个公交车站，第 $*i*$ 个车站与中央广场的距离为 $*a*_{*i*}$，所有距离均不相同。车站按照距广场距离递增的顺序编号，即对于从 1 到 $*n* - 1$ 的所有 $*i*$，均有 $*a*_{*i*} < *a*_{*i* + 1}$。公交车从第一个车站出发，依次经过车站 2、3 等。到达编号为 $*n*$ 的车站后，公交车掉头，沿相反方向驶向车站 1，并按逆序经过所有中间车站。之后，它再次向车站 $*n*$ 的方向行驶。在一天中，公交车会沿这条路线不间断地运行。

公交车配备了伯兰本地定位系统。当公交车经过某个车站时，系统会记录该车站的编号。

该系统的一项关键功能是，可以查询公交车在路径中某一对车站之间的部分所行驶的距离。系统的一个特殊模块接收路径某一段上车站集合的信息：公交车每经过某个车站一次，该车站编号就在集合中出现一次。该模块会返回所行驶路径的长度（如果无法唯一确定长度，则返回 -1）。但该模块的操作因以下事实而变得复杂：请求中的车站编号并不是按照经过顺序给出，而是按照非递减顺序给出。

例如，如果车站数量为 6，公交车路径的一段从车站 5 开始，在车站 3 结束，并依次经过以下车站：![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f603d9c4afa723f7976dfc0c5250bf25a325383b.png)，那么关于这段路径的请求将表示为：$3, 4, 5, 5, 6$。如果公交车在从车站 5 到车站 3 的这段路径中还来得及经过第 1 个车站（也就是说，我们考虑的路径段在从车站 5 出发前往车站 3 的途中，第二次经过车站 3 时结束），那么请求将表示为：$1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6$。

现在，你需要复现伯兰程序员的成果，实现这一功能。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 2·10^{5}$）——车站的数量。

第二行包含 $*n*$ 个整数（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$）——第 $*i*$ 个车站到中央广场的距离。第二行中的数字按递增顺序排列。

第三行包含一个整数 $*m*$（$1 ≤ *m* ≤ 4·10^{5}$）——公交车在路径的某一段中经过的车站数量。

第四行包含 $*m*$ 个整数（$1 ≤ *b*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$）——公交车在该路径段中经过的车站编号的有序列表。某个车站编号出现的次数，等于公交车经过该车站的次数。

保证该请求对应于路径上的某一段。

## 输出格式

请在一行中输出公交车行驶的距离。如果无法唯一确定该距离，则输出 $- 1$。 

## 说明

题面中的第一个测试对应于题目中展示的第一个例子。

题面中的第二个测试对应于题目中展示的第二个例子。

在第三个样例中，有两条可能的路径，且它们的长度不同，因此所求路径段的长度无法唯一确定。

在第四个样例中，尽管有两条不同的路径对应于该请求，但它们的长度相同，因此所求路径段的长度可以唯一确定。
